evidence.pali: ‘‘Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘aniccānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘aniccānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘virāgānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘virāgānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘nirodhānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘nirodhānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; dhammesu dhammānupassī, bhikkhave, tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. So yaṃ taṃ abhijjhādomanassānaṃ pahānaṃ taṃ paññāya disvā sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, dhammesu dhammānupassī tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.
evidence.chinese_simplified: 诸比丘，当比丘修学：‘我将随观无常而出息’，修学：‘我将随观无常而入息’；修学：‘我将随观离贪而出息’，修学：‘我将随观离贪而入息’；修学：‘我将随观灭而出息’，修学：‘我将随观灭而入息’；修学：‘我将随观舍遣而出息’，修学：‘我将随观舍遣而入息’时，诸比丘，在那时，比丘于诸法随观法而住，精勤、正知、具念，调伏世间的贪与忧。他以智慧见到那贪与忧的断除，并善加舍观。是故，诸比丘，在那时，比丘于诸法随观法而住，精勤、正知、具念，调伏世间的贪与忧。
evidence.english: When, monks, a monk trains thus: ‘Contemplating impermanence, I will breathe out,’ he trains thus: ‘Contemplating impermanence, I will breathe in’; he trains thus: ‘Contemplating dispassion, I will breathe out,’ he trains thus: ‘Contemplating dispassion, I will breathe in’; he trains thus: ‘Contemplating cessation, I will breathe out,’ he trains thus: ‘Contemplating cessation, I will breathe in’; he trains thus: ‘Contemplating relinquishment, I will breathe out,’ he trains thus: ‘Contemplating relinquishment, I will breathe in’; at that time, monks, a monk dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure for the world. Having seen with wisdom the abandoning of that covetousness and displeasure, he closely observes with equanimity. Therefore, monks, at that time a monk dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure for the world.

entries.pali: 236 . Aniccanti anupassī, aniccassa vā anupassanasīlo aniccānupassī ti ettha kiṃ panetaṃ aniccaṃ, kathaṃ vā aniccaṃ, kā vā aniccānupassanā, kassa vā aniccānupassanāti catukkaṃ vibhāvetabbanti taṃ dassento ‘‘aniccaṃ veditabba’’ ntiādimāha.
entries.chinese_simplified: 236. 随观为‘无常’者，或惯于随观无常法者，是为无常随观者。于此，‘此无常者为何？因何而为无常？何为无常随观？无常随观为谁所有？’——为阐明此四法，故说‘当知无常’等。
entries.english: 236. One who contemplates 'impermanent,' or one whose habit is to contemplate the impermanent, is called 'one who contemplates the impermanent.' Here, the tetrad—What is this 'impermanent'? How is it impermanent? What is the contemplation of impermanence? And whose is the contemplation of impermanence?—should be clarified. To show this, he said, 'The impermanent is to be known,' and so on.

entries.pali: Ettha ca pariññātaṃ tassāti ayaṃ vāro maggabhāvanāpāripūridassanatthaṃ vutto. Itare pana phalasacchikiriyāpāripūridassanatthanti veditabbā. Dvīhi vā kāraṇehi arahā na maññati vatthussa ca pariññātattā akusalamūlānañca samucchinnattā. Tenassa pariññātavārena vatthuno vatthupariññaṃ dīpeti, itarehi akusalamūlasamucchedanti. Tattha pacchimesu tīsu vāresu ayaṃ viseso veditabbo, tīsu hi vāresu rāge ādīnavaṃ disvā dukkhānupassī viharanto appaṇihitavimokkhena vimutto khayā rāgassa vītarāgo hoti. Dose ādīnavaṃ disvā aniccānupassī viharanto animittavimokkhena vimutto khayā dosassa vītadoso hoti. Mohe ādīnavaṃ disvā anattānupassī viharanto suññatavimokkhena vimutto khayā mohassa vītamoho hotīti.
entries.chinese_simplified: 于此，‘彼已遍知’此品是为了显示道的修习圆满而说。其余诸品则应理解为是为了显示果的作证圆满。或者，阿罗汉因二种原因而不思量：因事已被遍知，及因诸不善根已被断绝。因此，以遍知品阐明对事的遍知，以其余诸品阐明不善根的断绝。于后三品中，应知此差别：于此三品中，见贪之过患而住于苦随观者，以无愿解脱而解脱，因贪之尽而离贪；见瞋之过患而住于无常随观者，以无相解脱而解脱，因瞋之尽而离瞋；见痴之过患而住于无我随观者，以空解脱而解脱，因痴之尽而离痴。
entries.english: And here, this section 'it is fully understood by him' is stated to show the completion of the development of the path. The others, however, should be understood as for the purpose of showing the completion of the realization of the fruit. Or, an Arahant does not conceive for two reasons: because the basis has been fully understood and because the unwholesome roots have been eradicated. By that section on full understanding, it shows the full understanding of the basis for him; by the others, it shows the eradication of the unwholesome roots. In this context, this distinction in the last three sections should be understood: in these three sections, one who, having seen the danger in greed, abides contemplating suffering, is liberated by the desireless liberation; through the destruction of greed, he becomes free from greed. One who, having seen the danger in hatred, abides contemplating impermanence, is liberated by the signless liberation; through the destruction of hatred, he becomes free from hatred. One who, having seen the danger in delusion, abides contemplating not-self, is liberated by the emptiness liberation; through the destruction of delusion, he becomes free from delusion.

entries.pali: Sabbe dhammā nālaṃ abhinivesāyā ti ettha sabbe dhammā nāma pañcakkhandhā dvādasāyatanāni aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo. Te sabbepi taṇhādiṭṭhivasena abhinivesāya nālaṃ na pariyattā na samatthā na yuttā, kasmā? Gahitākārena atiṭṭhanato. Te hi niccāti gahitāpi aniccāva sampajjanti, sukhāti gahitāpi dukkhāva sampajjanti, attāti gahitāpi anattāva sampajjanti, tasmā nālaṃ abhinivesāya. Abhijānātī ti aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattāti ñātapariññāya abhijānāti. Parijānātī ti tatheva tīraṇapariññāya parijānāti. Yaṃkiñci vedana nti antamaso pañcaviññāṇasampayuttampi yaṃkiñci appamattakampi vedanaṃ anubhavati. Iminā bhagavā sakkassa devānamindassa vedanāvasena nibbattetvā arūpapariggahaṃ dasseti. Sace pana vedanākammaṭṭhānaṃ heṭṭhā na kathitaṃ bhaveyya, imasmiṃ ṭhāne kathetabbaṃ siyā. Heṭṭhā pana kathitaṃ, tasmā satipaṭṭhāne vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Aniccānupassī ti ettha aniccaṃ veditabbaṃ, aniccānupassanā veditabbā, aniccānupassī veditabbo. Tattha anicca nti pañcakkhandhā, te hi uppādavayaṭṭhena aniccā. Aniccānupassanā ti pañcakkhandhānaṃ khayato vayato dassanañāṇaṃ. Aniccānupassī ti tena ñāṇena samannāgato puggalo . Tasmā ‘‘aniccānupassī viharatī’’ti aniccato anupassanto viharatīti ayamettha attho.
entries.chinese_simplified: ‘一切法不适于执取’(Sabbe dhammā nālaṃ abhinivesāya)：此处‘一切法’是指五蕴、十二处、十八界。所有这些，都因贪爱与邪见而不适于执取，即不充足、不堪能、不适宜。为何？因为它们不以被执取的样子而住立。它们被执取为‘常’，却成为无常；被执取为‘乐’，却成为苦；被执取为‘我’，却成为无我，因此不适于执取。‘了知’(Abhijānāti)，即以知遍知(ñātapariññā)来了知无常、苦、无我。‘遍知’(Parijānāti)，即同样以审察遍知(tīraṇapariññā)来遍知。‘任何感受’(Yaṃkiñci vedanaṃ)，即体验任何微少的感受，乃至与五识相应的感受。世尊(bhagavā)以此为天帝释(Sakka devānaminda)开示了由感受所引生的对无色法(arūpa)的把握。如果感受业处在前面没有讲过，就应在此处讲述。但在前面已经讲过了，因此应只按照《念处经》(Satipaṭṭhāna)中所说的方法来理解。‘随观无常者’(Aniccānupassī)：于此，应知‘无常’、‘无常随观’和‘随观无常者’。其中，‘无常’是指五蕴，它们因生灭的特相而为无常。‘无常随观’是指见到五蕴消尽、坏灭的智。‘随观无常者’是指具足此智的个人(puggala)。因此，‘随观无常而住’(aniccānupassī viharati)，于此的含义是：随观其为无常而住。
entries.english: In the phrase, 'All phenomena are not fit for adherence': here, 'all phenomena' means the five aggregates, the twelve sense-bases, and the eighteen elements. All of these are not suitable, not sufficient, not capable, and not fit for adherence by way of craving and views. Why? Because they do not stand in the way they are grasped. Indeed, though grasped as 'permanent,' they become only impermanent; though grasped as 'pleasant,' they become only suffering; though grasped as 'self,' they become only not-self. Therefore, they are not fit for adherence. 'He knows directly' means he knows directly by the full understanding of the known that they are impermanent, suffering, and not-self. 'He fully understands' means he likewise fully understands by the full understanding of investigation. 'Whatever feeling' means he experiences any feeling whatsoever, even the slightest, associated with the five consciousnesses at the least. By this, the Blessed One, having caused it to arise by way of feeling for Sakka, lord of the devas, teaches the comprehension of the formless. If the meditation subject of feeling had not been spoken of below, it would have to be spoken of in this place. But it has been spoken of below; therefore, it should be understood according to the method stated in the Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta. In 'contemplating impermanence,' impermanence should be understood, the contemplation of impermanence should be understood, and the one who contemplates impermanence should be understood. Therein, 'impermanence' means the five aggregates; indeed, they are impermanent in the sense of arising and passing away. 'Contemplation of impermanence' is the knowledge of seeing the five aggregates in terms of destruction and vanishing. 'One who contemplates impermanence' is the person endowed with that knowledge. Therefore, in 'he dwells contemplating impermanence,' the meaning here is: he dwells contemplating as impermanent.

entries.pali: Ayañca rūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ kathetvā arūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ vedanāvasena nivattetvā desanā tathāvinetabbapuggalāpekkhāya suttantaresupi (dī. ni. 2.373; ma. ni. 1.106, 390, 413, 450, 465, 467; ma. ni. 2.306, 209; 3.67, 342; saṃ. ni. 4.248) āgatā evāti dassento ‘‘na kevala’’ ntiādimāha. Tattha mahāsatipaṭṭhāne (dī. ni. 2.273) tathā desanāya āgatabhāvo anantarameva āvi bhavissati, majjhimanikāye satipaṭṭhānadesanāpi (ma. ni. 1.106) tādisī eva. Cūḷataṇhāsaṅkhaye ‘‘evaṃ cetaṃ, devānaṃ inda, bhikkhuno sutaṃ hoti ‘sabbe dhammā nālaṃ abhinivesāyā’ti, so sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhijānāti , sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhiññāya sabbaṃ dhammaṃ parijānāti, sabbaṃ dhammaṃ pariññāya yaṃ kiñci vedanaṃ vedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, so tāsu vedanāsu aniccānupassī viharati, virāgānupassī’’tiādinā (ma. ni. 1.390) āgataṃ. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘arūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ vedanāvasena nivattetvā dassesī’’ ti. Mahātaṇhāsaṅkhaye pana ‘‘so evaṃ anurodhavirodhavippahīno yaṃ kiñci vedanaṃ vedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, so taṃ vedanaṃ nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṃ vedanaṃ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato yā vedanāsu nandī sā nirujjhatī’’tiādinā (ma. ni. 1.414) āgataṃ. Cūḷavedalle ‘‘kati panāyyevedanā’’tiādinā (ma. ni. 1.465) āgataṃ. Mahāvedalle ‘‘vedanāti, āvuso, vuccati, kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, ‘vedanā’ti vuccatī’’tiādinā (ma. ni. 1.450) āgataṃ. Evaṃ raṭṭhapālasuttādīsupi (ma. ni. 2.305) vedanākammaṭṭhānassa āgataṭṭhānaṃ uddharitvā vattabbaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 讲述了色业处之后，又以受为所缘来转入无色业处，为了教导适合不同根器的众生，这种说法也在其他的经中出现过（如长部2.373；中部1.106, 390, 413, 450, 465, 467；中部2.306, 209；3.67, 342；相应部4.248）。为了说明这一点，才说了“不仅如此”等。其中，这种说法在《大念处经》(Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta)中已经出现，下文即将阐明；《中部》的《念处经》(Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta)也是如此。在《小爱尽经》(Cūḷataṇhāsaṅkhayasutta)中记载：“诸天之主，比丘听闻‘一切法不应执取’，他就会遍知一切法，遍知一切法后，就会完全理解一切法，完全理解一切法后，他感受到的任何感受，无论是乐受、苦受还是不苦不乐受，他都会安住于随观诸受之无常，随观其离贪”等（中部1.390）。因此说“以受为所缘来显示无色业处”。在《大爱尽经》(Mahātaṇhāsaṅkhayasutta)中则说：“像这样，舍弃了顺从与违逆的人，感受任何感受，无论是乐受、苦受还是不苦不乐受，他不会欢喜、不会称赞、不会执著。因为不欢喜、不称赞、不执著，所以他对诸受的喜就会止息”等（中部1.414）。在《小韦达拉经》(Cūḷavedallasutta)中记载：“尊者，有多少种感受？”等（中部1.465）。在《大韦达拉经》(Mahāvedallasutta)中说：“贤友(āvuso)，所谓感受，究竟在什么情况下被称为感受？”等（中部1.450）。同样地，在《护国经》(Raṭṭhapālasutta)等（中部2.305）中，也应举出关于受业处的段落并加以说明。
entries.english: Having explained this meditation subject on form, and then reverting to the formless meditation subject by way of feeling, he says 'Not only...' and so forth, to show that such a teaching also occurs in other suttas, with reference to individuals to be trained in that way (Dī. Ni. 2.373; Ma. Ni. 1.106, 390, 413, 450, 465, 467; Ma. Ni. 2.306, 209; 3.67, 342; Saṃ. Ni. 4.248). Here, in the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta (Dī. Ni. 2.273), the occurrence of such a teaching will become evident immediately. Similarly, the teaching on the foundations of mindfulness in the Majjhima Nikāya (Ma. Ni. 1.106) is also of that kind. In the Cūḷataṇhāsaṅkhaya Sutta (Ma. Ni. 1.390), it occurs thus: 'Thus, O Sakka, lord of the devas, a bhikkhu hears: "All phenomena are not to be clung to." He directly knows all phenomena; having directly known all phenomena, he fully comprehends all phenomena; having fully comprehended all phenomena, whatever feeling he experiences—pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—he dwells contemplating impermanence in those feelings, contemplating dispassion,' and so forth. Therefore it is said, 'He showed the formless meditation subject by reverting to the aspect of feeling.' In the Mahātaṇhāsaṅkhaya Sutta (Ma. Ni. 1.414), it occurs thus: 'Thus, devoid of attraction and aversion, whatever feeling he experiences—pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—he does not delight in that feeling, welcome it, or remain holding to it. When he does not delight in that feeling, welcome it, or remain holding to it, the delight in feelings ceases,' and so forth. In the Cūḷavedalla Sutta (Ma. Ni. 1.465), it occurs thus: 'How many feelings are there, venerable sir?' and so forth. In the Mahāvedalla Sutta (Ma. Ni. 1.450), it occurs thus: 'Friend, it is called "feeling." But to what extent, friend, is it called "feeling"?' and so forth. Similarly, in the Raṭṭhapāla Sutta and others (Ma. Ni. 2.305), the passages where the meditation subject of feeling occurs should be extracted and stated.

entries.pali: ‘‘Yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu…pe… nibbānaṃ mābhinandī’’ti ayaṃ desanā. ‘‘Idha, devānaminda, bhikkhuno sutaṃ hoti ‘sabbe dhammā nālaṃ abhinivesāyā’ti, evañcetaṃ, devānaminda, bhikkhuno sutaṃ hoti ‘sabbe dhammā nālaṃ abhinivesāyā’ti, so sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhijānāti, sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhiññāya sabbaṃ dhammaṃ parijānāti, sabbaṃ dhammaṃ pariññāya yaṃ kiñci vedanaṃ vedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, so tāsu vedanāsu aniccānupassī viharati, virāgānupassī viharati, nirodhānupassī viharati, paṭinissaggānupassī viharatī’’ti (ma. ni. 1.390) imāya desanāya saṃsandati. ‘‘Yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṃ…pe… abhisambuddhoti vadāmī’’ti ayaṃ desanā ‘‘sutavā ca kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako…pe… sappurisadhamme suvinīto rūpaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati, vedanaṃ…pe…, saññaṃ…pe…, saṅkhāre…pe…, viññāṇaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Yampi taṃ diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā, tampi ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Yampi taṃ diṭṭhiṭṭhānaṃ, so loko so attā so pecca bhavissāmi ‘nicco dhuvo sassato api pariṇāmadhammo sassatisamaṃ tatheva ṭhassāmī’ti, tampi ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. So evaṃ samanupassanto na paritassatī’’ti (ma. ni. 1.241) evamādidesanāhi saṃsandatīti, ayaṃ catubyūho hāro .
entries.chinese_simplified: ‘诸比丘，即使是那位比丘……乃至……不应乐喜涅槃’，此为一教说。此教说与‘天帝释(Devānaminda)，在此，有比丘听闻：“一切法皆不应执取。”天帝释，既然该比丘如此听闻：“一切法皆不应执取”，他便证知一切法；证知一切法后，他遍知一切法；遍知一切法后，无论他感受到什么受——乐受、苦受或不苦不乐受——他都于那些受中安住于随观无常、随观离贪、随观灭、随观舍遣’（《中部》1.390）相连结。‘诸比丘，即使是那位阿罗汉比丘……乃至……我说他是正自觉者’，此为一教说。此教说与‘诸比丘，多闻的圣弟子……于善士法善受调伏，他审察色：“这不是我的，这不是我，这不是我的我。”他审察受……想……行……识：“这不是我的，这不是我，这不是我的我。”任何所见、所闻、所觉、所得、所寻求、为意所寻思者，他也审察：“这不是我的，这不是我，这不是我的我。”任何见的立足处，即“世界即我，我死后将是常、恒、久、不变易之法，我将如是永恒存续”，他也审察：“这不是我的，这不是我，这不是我的我。”如此审察，他便不忧虑’（《中部》1.241）等教说相连结。此为四严饰导引(catubyūho hāro)。
entries.english: “Even that bhikkhu, O bhikkhus… should not delight in Nibbāna,” this is the teaching. This connects with the teaching: “Here, O lord of devas, a bhikkhu has heard: ‘All things are not fit for clinging.’ When a bhikkhu has heard thus, ‘All things are not fit for clinging,’ he directly knows all things. Having directly known all things, he fully understands all things. Having fully understood all things, whatever feeling he feels—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—he dwells contemplating impermanence in those feelings, contemplating dispassion, contemplating cessation, contemplating relinquishment.” (MN 1.390) “Even that bhikkhu, O bhikkhus, who is an arahant… I declare him fully enlightened,” this is the teaching. This connects with such teachings as: “But the instructed noble disciple, O bhikkhus… well-trained in the Dhamma of the noble ones, regards form thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ He regards feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ And whatever is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought after, and examined by the mind—that too he regards thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ And even that standpoint of views: ‘This world is the self; after death I shall be permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change, I shall remain the same for ever and ever’—that too he regards thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Thus regarding, he is not agitated.” (MN 1.241) This is the fourfold guide.

entries.pali: Uppādavayaṭṭhenā ti udayabbayasabhāvena uppajjitvā nirujjhanena. Aniccā ti addhu vā. Aniccalakkhaṇaṃ aniccatā udayavayatā. Tasmā ti yasmā pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ khayato vayato dassanañāṇaṃ aniccānupassanā, taṃsamaṅgī ca puggalo aniccānupassī , tasmā. Khayavirāgo ti khayasaṅkhāto virāgo saṅkhārānaṃ palujjanā. Yaṃ āgamma sabbaso saṅkhārehi virajjanā hoti, taṃ nibbānaṃ accantavirāgo. Nirodhānupassimhipī ti nirodhānupassipadepi. ‘‘Eseva nayo’’ ti abhidisitvā taṃ ekadesena vivaranto ‘‘nirodhopi hi…pe… duvidhoyevā’’ ti āha. Sabbāsavasaṃvare vuttavossaggova idha ‘‘paṭinissaggo’’ti vuttoti dassento ‘‘paṭinissaggo vuccati vossaggo’’ tiādimāha. Pariccāgavossaggo vipassanā. Pakkhandanavasena appanato pakkhandanavossaggo maggo aññassa tadabhāvato. So ti maggo. Ārammaṇato ti kiccasādhanavasena ārammaṇakaraṇato. Evañhi maggato aññesaṃ nibbānārammaṇānaṃ pakkhandanavossaggābhāvo siddho hoti. Pariccajanena pakkhandanena cāti dvīhipi vā kāraṇehi . Sabbesaṃ khandhānaṃ vossajjanaṃ tappaṭibaddhasaṃkilesappahānena daṭṭhabbaṃ. Cittaṃ pakkhandatī ti maggasampayuttaṃ cittaṃ sandhāyāha. Ubhayampetaṃ vossajjanaṃ. Tadubhayasamaṅgī ti vipassanāsamaṅgī maggasamaṅgī ca. ‘‘Aniccānupassanāya niccasaññaṃ pajahatī’’tiādivacanato (paṭi. ma. 1.52) yathā vipassanāya kilesānaṃ pariccāgapaṭinissaggo labbhati, evaṃ āyatiṃ tehi kilesehi uppādetabbakhandhānampi pariccāgapaṭinissaggo vattabbo, pakkhandanapaṭinissaggo pana magge labbhamānāya ekantakāraṇabhūtāya vuṭṭhānagāminivipassanāya vasena veditabbo, magge pana tadubhayampi ñāyāgatameva nippariyāyatova labbhamānattā. Tenāha ‘‘tadubhayasamaṅgī puggalo’’ tiādi.
entries.chinese_simplified: “以生灭义”(uppādavayaṭṭhena)是指以生起后即坏灭的生灭自性。“无常”(anicca)即“非恒常”(addhuva)。无常相即无常性，是生灭的状态。“因此”是说：因为见到五蕴的毁坏与消逝之智是无常随观(aniccānupassanā)，具足此智的个体(puggala)是无常随观者，所以这么说。“灭尽离贪”(khayavirāgo)是指名为“灭尽”的离贪，即诸行的败坏。依靠它而能完全离于一切诸行者，即是涅槃，是究竟的离贪。在“灭随观者”(nirodhānupassī)的词条中也是如此。在指示“此理亦然”后，又部分地阐释说：“灭亦有……乃至……两种。”为了表明在“一切漏的防护”中所说的“舍离”(vossagga)在此处被称为“断舍”(paṭinissagga)，而说“断舍即是所谓的舍离”等。以舍弃方式的舍离是观(vipassanā)；以跃入并致力于它的方式的舍离是道(magga)，因为其他(法)没有此(功能)。“那”即是道。“作为所缘”是指通过把(涅槃)作为所缘来完成其作用。这样，除了道以外，其他以涅槃为所缘的(法)没有跃入的舍离，此理即成立。(舍离)通过舍弃与跃入这两种原因。一切蕴的舍离，应理解为断除与它们相关的烦恼。“心跃入”是指与道相应的心。这两种都是舍离。“具足此二者”是指具足观与道。根据“以无常随观舍断常想”等(《无碍解道》1.52)的文句，正如通过观可以获得对烦恼的舍弃断舍，同样，对于未来将由那些烦恼产生的诸蕴，也应说有舍弃断舍；而跃入的断舍，则应理解为通过在道中获得的、作为决定性原因的、导向出起的观。在道中，此二者都是理所当然的，因为是无保留地获得的。因此说“具足此二者的个体”等。
entries.english: “By the meaning of arising and passing away” means by the nature of arising and dissolving, by arising and ceasing. “Impermanent” means not lasting. The characteristic of impermanence is impermanence, arising and passing away. “Therefore” means: since the knowledge of seeing the decay and passing away of the five aggregates is the contemplation of impermanence, and the person endowed with it is one who contemplates impermanence, therefore. “Dispassion through decay” means this is dispassion designated as decay, the crumbling of formations. That on account of which there is complete dispassion towards all formations is Nibbāna, the ultimate dispassion. “Even in the contemplation of cessation” means also in the term ‘contemplation of cessation.’ Having indicated, “This is the method,” he explains it in part, saying: “For cessation, too … is twofold.” Showing that the relinquishment (vossagga) mentioned in the context of the restraint of all taints is here called “abandonment” (paṭinissagga), he says: “Abandonment is called relinquishment,” and so on. The relinquishment by giving up is insight. The relinquishment by plunging in is the path, because of its applying itself by way of plunging in, and because of the absence of this in anything else. That is the path. “As an object” means because of making it an object by way of accomplishing its function. For in this way it is established that, apart from the path, there is no relinquishment by plunging in for other things that have Nibbāna as their object. “By giving up and by plunging in” means or by both these reasons. The relinquishing of all the aggregates should be seen as the abandoning of the defilements connected with them. “The mind plunges in”: he says this referring to the mind associated with the path. Both these are relinquishment. “One endowed with both” means endowed with both insight and the path. From the statement, “Through the contemplation of impermanence, one abandons the perception of permanence,” etc., just as through insight the abandonment by giving up defilements is obtained, so too the abandonment by giving up the aggregates that would be produced by those defilements in the future is to be understood. The abandonment by plunging in, however, is to be understood by way of the insight leading to emergence, which is obtained in the path and is the exclusive cause. But in the path, both are obtained by right method, being obtained directly. Therefore, he said: “The person endowed with both,” etc.

entries.work_title: 阿毗达摩入门-名色分别 Abhidhammāvatāro-Nāmarūpaparicchedo
entries.pali: Vipassanāyaniccānu-gatattā hi visesato; Vipassanto aniccānu-passī sikkhati paṇḍito.
entries.chinese_simplified: 特别地，因观紧随无常，智者修习无常随观。
entries.english: Indeed, because insight is especially characterized by the pursuit of impermanence, the wise one trains, seeing with insight and contemplating impermanence.

entries.pali: Asubhe pavattaṃ asubhanti vā pavattaṃ bhāvanākammaṃ asubhakammaṃ, tadeva aññassa punappunaṃ uppajjanakassa kāraṇaṭṭhena ṭhānattā asubhakammaṭṭhānaṃ, ārammaṇaṃ vā asubhakammassa padaṭṭhānaṭṭhena ṭhānanti asubhakammaṭṭhānanti idha asubhajjhānaṃ, teneva ‘‘oḷārikārammaṇattā’’ ti vuttaṃ. Paṭivedhavasenā ti vitakkādiaṅgapaṭilābhavasena. Ārammaṇasantatāyā ti anukkamena santakālaṃ upādāya vuttakāyadarathappaṭipassaddhivasena nibbuto. Parikammaṃ vā ti kasiṇaparikammaṃ kira nimittuppādapariyosānaṃ. Tadā hi nirassādattā asantaṃ, appaṇihitañca. Yathā upacāre nīvaraṇavigamena, aṅgapātubhāvena ca santatā hoti, na tathā idha, idaṃ pana ‘‘ādisamannāhārato’’ ti vuttaṃ. Dutiyavikappe asecanako ti atittikaro, tena vuttaṃ ‘‘ojavanto’’ ti. Cetasikasukhaṃ jhānakkhaṇepi atthi, evaṃ santepi ‘‘ubhopi jhānā vuṭṭhitasseva gahetabbā’’ti vuttaṃ. Samathena sakasantāne avikkhambhite . Itarathā pāpakānaṃ jhānena sahuppatti siyā. Khandhādīnaṃ lokuttarapādakattā nibbedhabhāgiyaṃ, visesena yassa nibbedhabhāgiyaṃ hoti, taṃ sandhāya vā. ‘‘Aniccānupassītiādicatukkavasena anupubbena ariyamaggavuḍḍhippatto samucchindati, sesānametaṃ natthī’’ti likhitaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 于不净中转起，或作为不净而转起的修习业，即是不净业。此业因作为其他（禅那）一再升起的因而为‘处’，故称‘不净业处’；或所缘作为不净业的近因而为‘处’，故称‘不净业处’。此处即指不净禅，因此说‘以粗显为所缘故’。‘以通达故’，意即以获得寻等（禅）支故。‘所缘相续’，是指次第经历平静的时期，依所述之身热恼的止息而寂静。‘或遍作’，据说即是遍处遍作，以似相生起为终。此时，因无味故不寂静，亦不胜妙。犹如在近行定中，因五盖远离、禅支显现而得寂静，此处则不然，此乃所谓‘从最初作意’。在第二种解释中，‘令人不厌足的’（asecanaka）意为‘不会令人餍足的’，因此说‘有滋味的’（ojavanto）。心所乐在禅那刹那亦有，即便如此，仍说‘两种（乐）都应于出定后把握’。若未以止镇伏自相续，则诸恶法可能与禅那同时生起。蕴等因是出世间的足处，故属决择分；或特指对具有决择分之人而言。经载：‘以无常随观等四法，次第达到圣道增长者，能根除（烦恼），其余则无此能力。’
entries.english: The act of development that occurs in relation to the unattractive, or the act of development that occurs as 'unattractive', is the 'unattractive action'. That very action, because it stands as a cause for another consciousness that arises again and again, is the 'meditation subject of unattractive action'. Or, the object stands as a proximate cause for the unattractive action, thus it is the 'meditation subject of unattractive action'. Here, the unattractive jhāna is called the 'meditation subject of unattractive action'. For that very reason, it is said, 'Because of its gross object'. 'By way of penetration' means by way of the attainment of the factors beginning with applied thought. Regarding 'due to the continuity of the object', it is said, it seems, with reference to a peaceful time in sequence: by way of the calming of bodily distress, one is quenched. Or, 'preliminary work' is indeed the preliminary work on a kasiṇa, which culminates in the arising of the sign. For at that time, because of the absence of gratification, it is not peaceful and not sublime. Just as in access concentration it is peaceful through the removal of the hindrances and the manifestation of the factors, it is not so here. But this meditation, however, is spoken of as being peaceful and sublime 'from the initial application onwards'. In the second alternative, `asecanaka` means 'that which does not cause satiety'; therefore, it is said to be 'rich in flavor'. Mental happiness exists even at the moment of jhāna. Even so, it is said, 'Both bodily and mental happiness are to be grasped only by one who has emerged from jhāna'. When evil states in one's own continuity are unsuppressed by serenity. Otherwise, the co-arising of evil states with the jhāna would occur. Because the aggregates and so on are a basis for the supramundane, it is 'partaking of penetration'. Or, it is said with reference to one for whom it is especially 'partaking of penetration'. It is written: 'By way of the tetrad beginning with "contemplating impermanence," one who has successively attained growth in the noble path cuts off defilements. For the others, this is not so'.

entries.pali: Anāvaraṇā tīsu kālesu sabbattha appaṭihatavuttitāya, asādhāraṇā sabbadhammānaṃ niravasesahetupaccayapariggahavasena tesañca sabhāvakiccādiavatthāvisesādiparijānanena āyūhanavelāyameva taṃtaṃkammānaṃ taṃtaṃphalavisesahīnamajjhimapaṇītādivibhāgassa indriyabaddhesu anindriyabaddhesu ca atisukhumatirohitavidūravuttiatītānāgatādibhedabhinnānaṃ rūpadhammānaṃ taṃtaṃkāraṇasamavāyavibhāvaneneva taṃtaṃphalesu vaṇṇasaṇṭhānagandharasaphassādivisesassa niravasesato paṭivijjhanena veditabbā. Ayañca attho bhagavato anekadhātunānādhātulokaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇādivasena veditabbo. Yathā ca passantassā ti idaṃ rāgaggiādīhi lokasannivāsassa ādittatādiākāradassanaṃ bhagavato mahākaruṇokkamanupāyaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Taṃ pana bahukehi ākārehi passantānaṃ buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ sattesu mahākaruṇā okkamati. ‘‘Āditto lokasannivāso…pe… uyyutto…pe… payāto…pe… kummaggappaṭipanno…pe… upanīyati loko adhuvo…pe… atāṇo loko anabhissaro…pe… assako loko sabbaṃ pahāya gamanīyaṃ…pe… ūno loko atitto taṇhādāsoti passantānaṃ buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ sattesu mahākaruṇā okkamatī’’tiādinā (paṭi. ma. 1.117) paṭisambhidāmagge parosataṃ ākārehi dassitanti ganthavitthāraṃ pariharituṃ saṃvaṇṇayituñca upāyaṃ dassetuṃ āha ‘‘taṃ sabbaṃ paṭisambhidāmagge mahākaruṇāñāṇavibhaṅgavasena jānitabba’’ nti. Indriyaparopariyattaāsayānusaya yamakapāṭihāriya sabbaññutānāvaraṇañāṇāni sesāsādhāraṇañāṇāni. Tesampi hi vibhaṅgo ‘‘idha tathāgato satte passati apparajakkhe’’tiādinā (paṭi. ma. 1.111) paṭisambhidāmagge nānappakārena dassitoti purimanayeneva atidisati. Ādi -saddena tattha vibhattānaṃ paṭisambhidāsaccañāṇādīnaṃ saṅgaho katoti veditabbo.
entries.chinese_simplified: 应知，（佛陀的智慧）是无碍的(anāvaraṇā)，因其于三时、一切处的作用皆无障碍；是不共的(asādhāraṇā)，因其能无遗漏地把握一切法的因缘，并遍知其自性、作用等状态差别；因其能在造业之时，即辨别彼彼业的下、中、上等种种果报差别；因其能仅通过辨明彼彼因缘的和合，即无遗漏地洞见与根相系及不与根相系的、极微细、隐蔽、遥远、以及属于过去未来等不同色法的彼彼果报中色、形、香、味、触等差别。此义理亦应通过世尊如实了知多界、种种界世间的智慧等来理解。而‘如见者’一语，是就世尊见到世间为贪火等所燃等相，作为生起大悲心的方法而说。当诸佛世尊以多种相状见众生时，大悲心即会生起。如《无碍解道》(Paṭisambhidāmagga)中以百多种相状所示：‘见世间炽燃……策励……前往……行于邪道……世间被引向（死亡），是无常的……世间无归护处，无主宰……世间无所有，须舍弃一切而去……世间有缺，不满足，是渴爱之奴，诸佛世尊见此，遂于众生生起大悲心’等。为免长篇累牍并为示讲解之法，故说：‘此一切皆应依《无碍解道》之大悲智分别来了知’。根上下智(indriyaparopariyattañāṇa)、意乐随眠智(āsayānusayañāṇa)、双神变智(yamakapāṭihāriyañāṇa)、一切知智(sabbaññutāñāṇa)、无碍智(anāvaraṇañāṇa)是其余的不共智。对这些智慧的分别，也以‘于此，如来见有情尘垢少’等多种方式在《无碍解道》中有所开示，故以前述方式类推而知。应知，（前文）‘等’字，摄集了彼处所分别的无碍解、谛智等。
entries.english: It is unobstructed, because it functions unhindered in all situations in the three times. It is uncommon, because it is to be understood through its complete grasp of the causes and conditions of all phenomena without remainder; through its thorough understanding of their particular states such as their intrinsic nature and function; and through its penetration, without remainder, of the distinctions of inferior, middling, and superior results of those various kammas at the very moment of their accumulation, and of the distinctions in color, shape, smell, taste, touch, and so on, in their respective fruits, by analyzing the respective combinations of causes of material phenomena—whether bound to the sense faculties or not, and whether divided into such categories as the extremely subtle, the concealed, the remote, the past, and the future. This meaning should be understood by way of the Blessed One’s knowledge of the world with its many and diverse elements as it really is. The phrase 'of one who sees thus' is stated with reference to the arising of the Blessed One's great compassion as a means upon seeing that the world-abode is ablaze with the fire of lust and so on. For great compassion arises in the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, toward beings when they see in many ways. In the Paṭisambhidāmagga, this is shown in over a hundred ways, beginning: 'Great compassion arises in the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, toward beings when they see that the world-abode is ablaze… agitated… rushing… has entered a wrong path… the world is being led on, it is impermanent… the world is without a shelter, without a master… the world is helpless, one must go on leaving all behind… the world is deficient, insatiable, a slave to craving' (Paṭi. Ma. i, 117). To avoid textual prolixity and to show the method for commenting, it is said: 'All this should be known by way of the analysis of the knowledge of great compassion in the Paṭisambhidāmagga.' The knowledges of the superior and inferior faculties of others, of their dispositions and latent tendencies, of the twin miracle, of omniscience, and of the unobstructed—these are the remaining uncommon knowledges. Their analysis, too, is shown in the Paṭisambhidāmagga in various ways, beginning: 'Here, the Tathāgata sees beings with little dust in their eyes' (Paṭi. Ma. i, 111). Thus an extension is made by the previous method. It should be understood that by the word 'etc.,' the knowledges of the discriminations, the truths, and so on, which are analyzed there, are included.
